mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that prompts the Federal Reserve to adopt a more accommodative stance, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.5%, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and a contraction in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a weakening manufacturing sector that leads to reduced corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances during late-cycle expansions when INDPRO declines, or the regime-specific Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates robust economic growth that supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 expands, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflation that may lead to monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a rise in CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances when both FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-unemployment shock regime, a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a persistent labor market weakness that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances during the post-unemployment shock regime when UNRATE rises, or the regime-specific Rank IC is below 0.02.
